model_annotation: This bar chart illustrates the percentage change in several economic indicators across three time periods: the 2000s, the 2010s, and the 2020s. The horizontal axis represents the time periods, labeled “2000er Jahre”, “2010er Jahre”, and “2020er Jahre”, and is categorical. The vertical axis represents percentage change, labeled “Durchschnitte in %”, with a linear scale ranging from -2.0 to 6.0, with tick marks at 1.0-unit intervals. Four sets of bars are displayed for each time period, representing “Welt-BIP” (green), “Welthandel” (light green), “Export Deutschland” (blue), and “Industrieproduktion Deutschland” (light blue). Within each time period, the bars are grouped, with each color representing a different economic indicator. In the 2000s, the “Welt-BIP” bar reaches approximately 3.9%, “Welthandel” reaches 5.4%, “Export Deutschland” reaches 1.0%, and “Industrieproduktion Deutschland” reaches 2.2%. In the 2010s, the “Welt-BIP” bar reaches approximately 4.8%, “Welthandel” reaches 5.0%, “Export Deutschland” reaches 3.7%, and “Industrieproduktion Deutschland” reaches 2.7%. In the 2020s, the “Welt-BIP” bar reaches approximately 0.4%, “Welthandel” reaches 2.3%, “Export Deutschland” reaches -1.5%, and “Industrieproduktion Deutschland” reaches 2.0%. The bars are arranged chronologically from left to right, and no bars are visually emphasized.
